bekennen.et: From Middle High German bekennen, from Old High German bikennen, from Proto-West Germanic *bikannijan. Equivalent to be- + kennen. Cognates include Dutch bekennen, and English and Scots beken.

s: to make anxious or uneasy; to tighten with anxiety

beklemmen.et: From Middle High German beklemmen, from Old High German biklemmen, from Proto-West Germanic *biklammjan, equivalent to be- + klemmen. Cognate with German Low German beklemmen, Dutch beklemmen, West Frisian beklamme, beklamje, English beclam.

bekloppt.et: Past participle of the rarer verb bekloppen (“to hit on", "to percuss”), thus “insane as if beaten in the head”. Related to kloppen (“to hit”), the Central and German Low German form of klopfen (“to knock”).

bekehren.et: From Middle High German bekēren, from Old High German bikēren, from Proto-West Germanic *bikaizjan.

Bekanntmachung.et: bekannt + Machung, or substantivisation of bekanntmachen (“make public”).

bekunden.et: Borrowed from German Low German, from be- + kunden, Central German form of künden (“to announce, tell”).
